Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Exercises ./ledger against a fresh database and compares every command's exit code and standard\n# output with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/LayersTesting/bin/run.sh APP  from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a\n# SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory. Every run starts with `ledger init`, so the grader\n# never depends on prior state. Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/seed_accounts.csv\" ]; then SEED=$HERE; else SEED=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nLEDGER=\"$APP/ledger\"\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nDATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL:-$WORK/ledger.db}\nexport DATABASE_URL\n\nif [ ! -x \"$LEDGER\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./ledger at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <ledger args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$LEDGER\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: ledger $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: ledger $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. Schema lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck A1 0 init < /dev/null\ncheck A2 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,0\ncategories,0\ntransactions,0\nEOF\n\n# ── B. Bulk load of the known dataset ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck B1 0 load accounts \"$SEED/seed_accounts.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\naccounts,4\nEOF\ncheck B2 0 load categories \"$SEED/seed_categories.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\ncategories,7\nEOF\ncheck B3 0 load transactions \"$SEED/seed_transactions.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\ntransactions,120\nEOF\ncheck B4 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,4\ncategories,7\ntransactions,120\nEOF\n\n# ── C. Reports over the seeded rows ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck C1 0 report balances <<'EOF'\naccount,name,transactions,balance\nDRAWER1,Front Drawer,39,2299.38\nDRAWER2,Back Drawer,39,1378.32\nPETTY,Petty Cash,21,306.25\nSAFE,Store Safe,21,250.00\nTOTAL,,120,4233.95\nEOF\ncheck C2 0 report categories <<'EOF'\ncategory,description,transactions,inflow,outflow,net\nOPENING,Opening balance,2,5200.00,0.00,5200.00\nPAYROLL,Payroll,6,0.00,7200.00,-7200.00\nREFUND,Customer refunds,12,0.00,101.25,-101.25\nRENT,Rent,3,0.00,2700.00,-2700.00\nSALES,Sales receipts,64,9578.95,0.00,9578.95\nSUPPLY,Supplies,15,0.00,543.75,-543.75\nTRANSFER,Internal transfer,18,5100.00,5100.00,0.00\nTOTAL,,120,19878.95,15645.00,4233.95\nEOF\ncheck C3 0 report monthly <<'EOF'\nmonth,transactions,inflow,outflow,net\n2026-01,40,9659.45,5215.00,4444.45\n2026-02,40,4979.65,5215.00,-235.35\n2026-03,40,5239.85,5215.00,24.85\nTOTAL,120,19878.95,15645.00,4233.95\nEOF\n\n# ── D. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope. Each command module registers its handlers here at import time.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom cli.errors import Usage\n\nHandler = Callable[[object, list[str]], list[list[str]]]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Command:\n    \"\"\"One registered command: the words that name it, its argument bounds, and its handler.\"\"\"\n\n    path: tuple[str, ...]\n    min_args: int\n    max_args: int\n    handler: Handler\n\n\nCOMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], Command] = {}\n\n\ndef register(path: Sequence[str], min_args: int, max_args: int, handler: Handler) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Register ``handler`` for the command words ``path``.\n\n    ``handler(db, args)`` returns the header row followed by the data rows. Registering the same\n    path twice is a programming error and raises ``ValueError``.\n    \"\"\"\n    key = tuple(path)\n    if not key:\n        raise ValueError(\"a command path needs at least one word\")\n    if key in COMMANDS:\n        raise ValueError(f\"command {' '.join(key)!r} is already registered\")\n    COMMANDS[key] = Command(key, min_args, max_args, handler)\n\n\ndef resolve(argv: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[Command, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Find the command named by the leading words of ``argv`` and check its argument count.\n\n    Raises ``Usage`` for no command, an unknown command, or a wrong argument count. Nothing is\n    opened or written here.\n    \"\"\"\n    matches = [command for key, command in COMMANDS.items() if tuple(argv[: len(key)]) == key]\n    if not matches:\n        raise Usage(\"unknown command: \" + (\" \".join(argv) if argv else \"(none)\"))\n    command = max(matches, key=lambda item: len(item.path))\n    args = list(argv[len(command.path) :])\n    if not command.min_args <= len(args) <= command.max_args:\n        raise Usage(f\"{' '.join(command.path)} takes {command.min_args} to {command.max_args} arguments\")\n    return command, args\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":834,"cache_read_input_tokens":76900,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":834},"output_tokens":16,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"2b71fc6d-011a-4cb4-99b8-9dde1a2ddbf2","uuid":"b2168819-3333-425b-99c6-6cb339890556","timestamp":"2026-10-25T18:17:36.331Z","request_id":"req_011CgPQzEV4X4NvrxVfav6Ug","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01Wg5bxsGmYMertY3pjtGM3J":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261025.175746/build/LayersTesting/cli/registry.py","content":"\"\"\"The command table. Each command module registers its handlers here at import time.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom cli.errors import Usage\n\nHandler = Callable[[object, list[str]], list[list[str]]]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Command:\n    \"\"\"One registered command: the words that name it, its argument bounds, and its handler.\"\"\"\n\n    path: tuple[str, ...]\n    min_args: int\n    max_args: int\n    handler: Handler\n\n\nCOMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], Command] = {}\n\n\ndef register(path: Sequence[str], min_args: int, max_args: int, handler: Handler) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Register ``handler`` for the command words ``path``.\n\n    ``handler(db, args)`` returns the header row followed by the data rows. Registering the same\n    path twice is a programming error and raises ``ValueError``.\n    \"\"\"\n    key = tuple(path)\n    if not key:\n        raise ValueError(\"a command path needs at least one word\")\n    if key in COMMANDS:\n        raise ValueError(f\"command {' '.join(key)!r} is already registered\")\n    COMMANDS[key] = Command(key, min_args, max_args, handler)\n\n\ndef resolve(argv: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[Command, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Find the command named by the leading words of ``argv`` and check its argument count.\n\n    Raises ``Usage`` for no command, an unknown command, or a wrong argument count. Nothing is\n    opened or written here.\n    \"\"\"\n    matches = [command for key, command in COMMANDS.items() if tuple(argv[: len(key)]) == key]\n    if not matches:\n        raise Usage(\"unknown command: \" + (\" \".join(argv) if argv else \"(none)\"))\n    command = max(matches, key=lambda item: len(item.path))\n    args = list(argv[len(command.path) :])\n    if not command.min_args <= len(args) <= command.max_args:\n        raise Usage(f\"{' '.join(command.path)} takes {command.min_args} to {command.max_args} arguments\")\n    return command, args\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Wg5bxsGmYMertY3pjtGM3J","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Each returns its value or raises ``Rejected``.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom datetime import date\n\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\nCODE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z0-9]{1,12}\")\nDATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n# Commas would split a CSV field and line breaks would split a row, so neither may appear in text.\nFORBIDDEN_TEXT = (\",\", \"\\n\", \"\\r\")\n\n\ndef validate_code(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An account or category code: 1 to 12 characters from ``A-Z`` and ``0-9``.\"\"\"\n    if not CODE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise Rejected(f\"code must be 1 to 12 characters from A-Z and 0-9: {text!r}\")\n    return text\n\n\ndef validate_name(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A name: 1 to 40 characters, with no comma or line break.\"\"\"\n    return _validate_text(\"name\", text, 1, 40)\n\n\ndef validate_memo(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A memo: 0 to 60 characters, with no comma or line break.\"\"\"\n    return _validate_text(\"memo\", text, 0, 60)\n\n\ndef validate_date(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A real calendar date written ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    if DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        try:\n            date.fromisoformat(text)\n            return text\n        except ValueError:\n            pass\n    raise Rejected(f\"date must be a real calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD: {text!r}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_text(label: str, text: str, minimum: int, maximum: int) -> str:\n    if not minimum <= len(text) <= maximum:\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must be {minimum} to {maximum} characters\")\n    if any(mark in text for mark in FORBIDDEN_TEXT):\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must not contain a comma or line break\")\n    return text\n"}}}

test_handler_error_exits_with_its_code_and_writes_nothing(scratch_command, monkeypatch, tmp_path):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", str(tmp_path / \"ledger.db\"))\n\n    def handler(db, {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgPR6Qn6zQv83WU3pGyp1","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"RESULT: SUCCESS\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- ledger\n- cli/__init__.py\n- cli/__main__.py\n- cli/database.py\n- cli/errors.py\n- cli/money.py\n- cli/output.py\n- cli/registry.py\n- cli/testing.py\n- cli/validate.py\n- cli/commands/__init__.py\n- tests/test_cli_foundation.py\n- pyproject.toml\n\nSUMMARY:\nThe cli-foundation story is built. The database story needed no writes in this step: `persistence/`, `schema.sql`, and `schema-verification.json` were already generated, and `DATABASE.md` lives in the protected Target blueprint, so I did not author it.\n\n- **`ledger`**: a POSIX sh launcher. It uses `.venv/bin/python` when present, otherwise `python3`, and runs `python -m cli` with the build root on `PYTHONPATH`. It contains no logic and is executable.\n- **Dispatch (`cli/__init__.py`, `cli/registry.py`)**: `main(argv) -> int` resolves the longest registered command path and checks argument count before opening the database. A `LedgerError` maps to its exit code. A `PersistenceError` maps to 1. Diagnostics go to stderr as one line. The handler runs to completion before any CSV is written.\n- **Errors (`cli/errors.py`)**: `Operational` (1), `Usage` (2), `Rejected` (3), `NotFound` (4).\n- **Output (`cli/output.py`)**: `write_rows` writes comma-separated lines with `\\n` endings and no quoting. `TRANSACTION_HEADER` and `format_transaction` produce the six declared fields.\n- **Money (`cli/money.py`)**: integer-cent parsing and two-decimal formatting. Zero, extra decimals, signs other than a leading `-`, and comma forms are rejected.\n- **Validators (`cli/validate.py`)**: codes, names, memos, and dates, each returning its value or raising `Rejected`.\n- **Store location (`cli/database.py`)**: `DATABASE_URL`, then `DATABASE_PATH`, then `data/app.db`, opened via `persistence.open_database`.\n- **In-process runner (`cli/testing.py`)**: `cli_runner(*args)` returns `(code, stdout, stderr)`.\n- **Command loader (`cli/commands/__init__.py`)**: imports every module in the package at startup so command modules self-register.\n\nChoices I made, for you to redirect:\n1. No commands are registered yet. Every command currently exits 2 as an unknown command. The command stories will register their handlers.\n2. Names and memos also reject `\\r`, not only `\\n`, because a carriage return would also break a CSV line.\n3.
